name: Greek nationalism
summary: Greek nationalism is the nationalism of Greeks and Greek culture, which became a major political movement in the early nineteenth century. It centres on the unity and freedom of the Greek nation, continuity from ancient Greece and Byzantium, the Orthodox Church as a marker of identity, and, historically, the Megali Idea of uniting Greek lands in one state. Since 1923 its mainstream form has been defensive, focused on borders, Cyprus, the Aegean, heritage and naming disputes.
scope: Mainstream Greek nationalism from the 1821 revolution and the Kolettis-era Megali Idea through the Venizelist expansion to the post-1974 defensive nationalism of the Greek right (as documented for the Macedonia naming dispute and Cyprus). It excludes the neo-Nazi strand of Golden Dawn and treats the Metaxas regime as a variant. The sources are silent on economic and social policy, so many such answers are low-confidence inferences.

keyFigures.name: Ioannis Kolettis
keyFigures.role: Prime minister whose 1844 speech gave the Megali Idea its name.

keyFigures.name: Eleftherios Venizelos
keyFigures.role: Leader of the national liberation movement who expanded Greece in the Balkan Wars.

keyFigures.name: Ioannis Metaxas
keyFigures.role: Led the 4th of August Regime (1936-41), in which Greek nationalism was the main ideology.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Greek nationalism is a program about nation and territory; the sources assign it no settled health policy, and nationalist parties range from state welfare to market views.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Nothing in the nationalist sources addresses wage floors; adherents split along their parties' general economic lines.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The article's sidebar lists both private property and a social market economy alongside protectionism, so the tradition is not committed either way.

public-ownership.rationale: Nationalist parties on the Greek right are listed with private property and a social market economy, which leans against broad public ownership, though strategic-asset nationalism exists.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The ideology is indifferent on tax progressivity; its economic position varies by party.

unions-good.rationale: No nationalist source takes a stance on unions; adherents are split between labour-friendly and employer-friendly parties.

property-fundamental.rationale: Private property appears among the principles listed for the Greek right-wing nationalist milieu, so adherents mostly accept it as a strong right.

cut-welfare.rationale: Not a nationalist question in the sources; nationalists are split, though many tie welfare to citizens only.

worker-ownership.rationale: Worker ownership is a socialist demand outside the nationalist program, which lists private property as a principle.

strong-leader.rationale: The Metaxas 4th of August regime made Greek nationalism its main ideology, and the Megali Idea tradition valued decisive leadership, but mainstream adherents today are parliamentary.

state-harmful.rationale: Greek nationalism is built around creating and enlarging a Greek state, as the Megali Idea's aim of uniting all Greeks in one state shows.

limit-guns.rationale: No relevant position in the sources.

decide-locally.rationale: Kolettis stressed one state, one constitution and one religion for the nation, and the tradition centres on a unitary national state.

rehabilitation.rationale: Nothing in the sources; adherents split.

more-religion-public.rationale: Orthodoxy is the constitution's prevailing religion and the flag's cross symbolises it, so nationalists want Orthodoxy visible in public life.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not an issue the tradition addresses; the national-unity emphasis leans against group-based remedies.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Greek nationalism is defined as the nationalism of Greeks and Greek culture, and the language, Orthodox and heritage disputes in the sources are all about preserving it.

gradual-change.rationale: The tradition was revolutionary in 1821 yet conservative in the Orthodox and Metapolitefsi parties, so adherents are split.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Greek nationalists resisted outside settlement of the Macedonia name and view foreign bodies sceptically, though Greece itself is in the EU and NATO.

free-trade.rationale: Protectionism is listed beside a social market economy in the sidebar, so the tradition has no single line.

nation-first.rationale: Greek governments and parties placed the national claim over international pressure in the Macedonia dispute, including the 1994 embargo and the NATO veto threat.

open-borders.rationale: Nationhood is defined by Greek ethnicity and Orthodoxy and the project was to fix a Greek state's borders, so open borders contradict it.

revolution-justified.rationale: The movement's founding act was the 1821 revolution against Ottoman rule, which the Epidaurus declaration calls a national and sacred war to regain rights.

central-planning.rationale: The sidebar's private property and social market economy do not support central planning.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The sidebar lists protectionism among the principles linked to the milieu, but adherents are not uniform on it.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The sidebar lists private property and a market economy; abolishing money and wages is foreign to the tradition.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: No position in the sources; the tradition does not call for abolishing them.

one-party-rule.rationale: Only the Metaxas regime (1936-41) governed without parties; the mainstream nationalist parties listed compete in elections.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Early Greek nationalists served a monarchy and Kolettis argued with King Otto, but the republic's form is now settled and unamendable, so adherents are split.

democracy-best.rationale: Mainstream nationalists accept the parliamentary republic of the constitution, though Metaxas and Golden Dawn rejected parliamentary democracy.

workers-councils.rationale: The tradition is nationalist and property-respecting; council rule is a socialist demand.

right-to-secede.rationale: Greek nationalists treat national territory as unified and rejected minority claims, as in the Macedonia dispute.

political-violence-never.rationale: Grivas's EOKA fought British rule in Cyprus and the 1821 war was a violent liberation struggle, so mainstream adherents accept some violence.

war-builds-character.rationale: The Megali Idea took the nation through wars, but sources do not show adherents praising war itself.

separate-church-state.rationale: Article 3 names Orthodoxy the prevailing religion and the flag's cross symbolises it, so nationalists oppose strict separation.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Orthodoxy is the prevailing religion but the constitution is secular law, and the tradition has not sought scriptural law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The tradition is built on the state's role in defending and uniting the nation.

military-superiority.rationale: The Aegean and Cyprus disputes with Turkey make military strength a nationalist priority.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Greek nationalism treats the nation as Greeks, with interwar nationalists seeking to assimilate Orthodox Albanians, Aromanians and Bulgarians.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The tradition sees history as the continuity of the Greek nation, Byzantium and Hellenism, not class conflict.

civilizational-union.rationale: The Megali Idea aimed to unite Orthodox Greek lands under a revived Byzantine state, though the target was Greeks not all Orthodox.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The Epidaurus text tells the people to be docile to the Laws and treats the war as a collective national duty, but this is not a rights doctrine.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: No position in the sources; the tradition is not primitivist.

accelerate-technology.rationale: No position; the tradition emphasises heritage over disruption.

restore-past-order.rationale: The Megali Idea sought to restore Byzantium, a lost Greek empire, so a lost order carries weight, though the tradition also pursued modern state-building.

results-over-ideology.rationale: No position; nationalists place national ideals above pragmatism.

direct-action.rationale: The mainstream parties work through elections, though the movement's origins were insurrectionary.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Foreign to a tradition built on Hellenic civilisation and state-building.

production-for-use.rationale: A socialist principle; the tradition lists private property and a market economy.

profit-exploitation.rationale: A Marxist claim at odds with the tradition's listed private property and market principles.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: A Marxist doctrine opposed to the tradition's nationalism and property views.

collective-farming.rationale: Opposed to private property, which the tradition lists as a principle.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: A Marxist claim; the tradition explains wars through national conflict, as with Greece and Turkey.

taxation-theft.rationale: Not a nationalist claim; the tradition relies on a strong state.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The Epidaurus declaration speaks of the rights of the nation as a collective, regaining national rights alongside personal liberty.

conscription.rationale: Greece has long kept conscription and nationalists back it for defence against Turkey.

exit-over-voice.rationale: No position; the tradition emphasises rootedness.

state-as-business.rationale: The tradition treats the state as the nation's instrument, not a business.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Greek nationalism is mostly cultural-linguistic and Orthodox in its definition; racial science belongs to fringe strands like Golden Dawn.

organic-representation.rationale: Metaxas's regime had corporatist elements but mainstream adherents back party representation.

total-state.rationale: Only the Metaxas regime approached this, and mainstream adherents do not hold it.

national-rebirth.rationale: The Megali Idea and the 1821 revolution are framed as national revival after Ottoman rule, and the Metaxas regime used a rebirth rhetoric.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Historic Greek nationalism pursued expansion through the Megali Idea until 1922; modern adherents defend borders instead, so adherents split.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: A postmodern claim not made in the sources.

revive-national-language.rationale: Katharevousa was an attempt to bring written Greek closer to the ancient language; the question was settled for Demotic in 1976 so adherents are split.

national-self-determination.rationale: The Epidaurus declaration frames the war as the Greek nation regaining its rights, and the movement's purpose was a Greek state.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Orthodoxy is central to national identity as the prevailing religion.

class-collaboration.rationale: Nationalism subordinates class to the nation, as the Metaxas regime's national unity rhetoric shows.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The Macedonia dispute centred on defending Greek heritage such as the Vergina Sun and Alexander, and the tradition is built on Hellenic heritage.

workers-nation.rationale: The tradition places workers within the national community rather than an international class.

ban-interest.rationale: The tradition lists private property and a market economy.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Greek nationalism has not sought racial separation by law; Golden Dawn is a fringe exception.

state-class-instrument.rationale: A Marxist claim; the tradition sees the state as the nation's expression.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Interwar nationalists sought to assimilate Orthodox Albanians, Aromanians and Bulgarians, and the Orthodox Greek cultural nation is the model.

elite-replacement.rationale: A fringe claim mostly associated with ultranationalist parties; not mainstream.

national-mission.rationale: Kolettis said modern Greeks were destined to enlighten the East, but the claim concerns culture not government forms.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Populist nationalist parties say yes, while governing nationalists such as New Democracy do not.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The tradition uses the state to defend and promote the nation, so a minimal state is too narrow.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The tradition's membership is cultural, in that Orthodox assimilation was the goal, though Golden Dawn differs.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The article notes assimilationist and superiority claims in some strands, but mainstream adherents accept constitutional equality.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist debate foreign to the tradition.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Orthodoxy is the prevailing religion and proselytism has been restricted in Greece, but the sources do not tie that to nationalism.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: An Indian issue with no relevance to Greek nationalism.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist idea foreign to the tradition.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The Epidaurus text derives national authority from the people's regained rights and Article 1 declares all powers derive from the people.

population-transfer.rationale: The 1923 Greek-Turkish population exchange ended the Megali Idea and was accepted by Greece, but nationalists did not generally promote it.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Adherents accept force for national liberation and defence, as in 1821 and EOKA.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Golden Dawn was prosecuted and banned in effect, but nationalists are split on banning parties.

separated-powers.rationale: The Greek constitution is a parliamentary system and mainstream nationalism works within it.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Ethnic nationalism holds that a single Orthodox Greek culture binds the nation, so diversity is seen as weakening it.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The Metaxas regime suspended protections; mainstream adherents work in a constitutional republic.

party-controls-media.rationale: Only authoritarian strands such as Metaxas controlled the media; mainstream nationalists do not.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Greece joined the EU, but nationalist parties oppose ceding sovereignty, as the Macedonia dispute's EC-recognition fight shows.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The Orthodox Church is episcopal and a national church linked to Greek identity under Article 3.

clerical-rule.rationale: Orthodoxy is a prevailing religion but clergy do not rule in the Greek state.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Greece is in NATO and nationalists want allies against Turkey, though some are anti-NATO.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not a nationalist position; contradicts private property.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The Megali Idea and enosis aimed to unite Greek-populated lands in one state, including Cyprus, which the sources call a major demand.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The article notes ancient and later claims of Greek superiority and treats Hellenic culture as foundational.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Greek nationalism defines the nation as ethnic Greeks and links diaspora, so descent is the basis.

minority-language-support.rationale: Greek nationalists treated the Slavic-speaking minority as unrelated and resisted using Macedonian identity, so mainstream adherents oppose it.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Epidaurus declaration centres on political independence and rights, not economic transformation.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The 1822 national assembly at Epidaurus drafted the founding constitution, a precedent adherents cite.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Greek nationalists reject territorial concessions to Turkey, and Cyprus and Aegean positions are treated as non-negotiable.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Greek nationalists call the Turkish presence in northern Cyprus after 1974 an invasion and occupation.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Orthodoxy is the prevailing religion and the Church is part of national identity.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The tradition rejects secession and minority claims on national territory.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The tradition favours a unitary Greek nation-state.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Foreign to modern Greek nationalism; the Byzantine emperor myth is nostalgia, not doctrine.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The Epidaurus text calls on the people to submit to the laws and the movement adopted constitutions from 1822.

leader-cult.rationale: The Metaxas regime promoted a leader cult, but mainstream adherents do not.

land-redistribution.rationale: The tradition lists private property and has no redistribution program.

refugee-return.rationale: Greek nationalists after 1922 and 1974 sought redress for expelled Greeks, including Cypriot refugees, but the sources do not detail this.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The Megali Idea claimed territory because Greeks lived there, but it ended after 1922 and modern mainstream adherents disclaim claims.

common-currency.rationale: Greece adopted the euro, but nationalists are split on the single currency.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The Megali Idea aimed to unite Greeks, but Greek nationalism has not pursued union with other kin peoples.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Nationalists resist giving minorities, such as the Slavic-speaking one, separate institutions.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The tradition holds ideas and national identity drive history, as with the Megali Idea.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Protectionism appears in the sidebar but a closed colonial bloc is foreign to the tradition.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: EOKA under Grivas was a small armed group that fought British rule in Cyprus.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Greek nationalism builds the national narrative from ancient Greece and Byzantium, and heritage is central to the Macedonia dispute.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Kolettis said modern Greeks would enlighten the East, but the sources do not support colonial tutelage.

patriotic-education.rationale: Nationalist movements teach national pride and the flag, whose cross symbolises Orthodoxy.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The Megali Idea sought to revive the Byzantine Empire's sphere, and Greek cultural influence in Anatolia and Constantinople was central.

delink-world-market.rationale: No position; the tradition does not call for delinking.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist claim foreign to the tradition.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The Greek constitution entrenches rights, but the sources do not tie that to nationalism.

elective-rulers.rationale: The republic is settled and the form of the State is unamendable, but early nationalists served a monarchy.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The Epidaurus text claims the right to regain rights from a despotic rule.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The constitution is parliamentary, but no nationalist source discusses it.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Nationalism calls for active participation in the national cause.

native-born-offices.rationale: The 1844 debate divided natives and immigrant Greeks over public office, and the question was contested among nationalists.

return-lost-territory.rationale: The Megali Idea claimed lost territory, but since 1923 Greece accepted the Lausanne borders, so adherents split over Asia Minor and Constantinople.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The Greek military has intervened in politics, but nationalists are split.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Protectionism appears in the sidebar but the sources do not specify.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Private property is a listed principle.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The Epidaurus declaration told the people to be submissive to the laws.

non-intervention.rationale: Greece's liberation depended on foreign involvement and the Cyprus case involves intervention claims.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Fringe nationalism alleges plots, but the sources do not document a mainstream view.

informal-organisation.rationale: Foreign to the tradition, which uses parties and the state.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Greek nationalists resisted outside settlement of the name dispute and treat national claims as primary.

religious-nation.rationale: The flag's cross symbolises Orthodoxy and interwar nationalists saw Orthodox groups as assimilable into the nation.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The tradition favours a unitary state.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Private property is a listed principle.

religion-illusion.rationale: Orthodoxy is the prevailing religion and central to identity.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: A socialist-feminist claim not made in the sources.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Katharevousa purification removed vulgar and foreign elements, but Demotic prevailed in 1976, so adherents split.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The Metaxas regime claimed a third way, but mainstream adherents back a market economy.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Only fringe nationalists such as Golden Dawn deny it; the sources document no mainstream denial.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Greece decriminalised it and mainstream nationalism does not demand criminalisation.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The mainstream nationalists compete in parliament, though Metaxas suppressed opposition.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: An Islamic doctrine foreign to the tradition.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: An Islamist doctrine foreign to the tradition.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: A modern progressive claim not made in the sources.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxist claim not made in the sources.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Orthodoxy is prevailing but Article 1 says all powers derive from the People.

social-market-economy.rationale: A social market economy is listed in the sidebar of principles in the Greek right-wing milieu.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The Aegean and Cyprus disputes make a strong military a core concern.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Greece is in NATO and nationalists want allies against Turkey, though some are anti-NATO.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Post-2010 nationalist parties opposed austerity, but mainstream ones accepted it, so adherents split.

property-franchise.rationale: The Epidaurus text speaks of rights for the whole people.

domination-women-nature.rationale: An ecofeminist claim not made in the sources.

reification.rationale: A Marxist claim not made in the sources.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The Epidaurus text stresses submission to laws, and the constitutional order is core to the state.

racial-franchise.rationale: Greek nationalism did not limit the vote by race.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Fringe nationalists have done this, but sources do not show a mainstream view.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The tradition relies on state authority.

abolish-ip.rationale: Private property is a listed principle.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The Metaxas regime had a youth organisation, but mainstream adherents do not.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Nationalists are split between anti-NATO and pro-ally strands.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Nationalist memory-making drove the construction of the Greek genocide as a historical fact, and nationalists seek its recognition.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Greek nationalism links ancient Greece, Byzantium and the modern state as one nation, with Byzantine emperors described as Greek.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The movement was born in armed revolution (1821) and its defensive nationalism relies on military defence, so lethal force is accepted.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Mainstream Greek nationalism is a state-centred cause of borders, heritage and Cyprus; the sources show no good-versus-evil framing.

second-chamber.rationale: Greece has a unicameral parliament under its constitution and nationalism has no settled view on a second chamber.

person-over-state.rationale: Nationalism puts the nation first, but Greek tradition also holds liberal constitutional rights; adherents are split.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The Orthodox Church is a core marker of Greek national identity, so a spiritual nature to politics is the documented majority view.

racial-pride.rationale: Pride in descent from ancient Greece and Byzantium is central to Greek nationalism, though framed as cultural continuity.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: After 1923 mainstream Greek nationalism gave up the Megali Idea and became defensive, centred on borders, Cyprus and the Aegean.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The language question and Kolettis's 'Greeks within and beyond the kingdom' make shared language and history central to Greek nationhood, though Orthodoxy is a second marker.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Greek nationalism treats military service and defence of the nation and its borders as a duty, so refusing orders is rejected.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The sources are silent on labour policy; the nationalist right and left have differed.

sacred-nation.rationale: Greek nationalism roots the nation in continuity from ancient Greece and Byzantium and Orthodoxy, treating it as an enduring community that gives lives meaning; the 1822 Epidauros declaration invokes the nation's eternal rights.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Greek nationalists have asserted heritage claims over names, but the sources do not settle whether regional varieties count as one language; no clear lean.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Nationalist parties split on labour law, and the sources give the Greek nationalist programme no position on union membership.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The Constitution names Eastern Orthodoxy the prevailing religion of Greece, so Greek nationalism gives one confession legal precedence.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: The Orthodox Church is treated as a marker and guardian of Greek identity, so nationalists reject blaming religion for women's oppression.

indirect-election.rationale: Article 1 of the constitution vests sovereignty in the people, and Greek nationalism has been tied to popular sovereignty since 1822.

national-church-status.rationale: Orthodoxy is treated as a marker of Greek nationhood and Article 3 gives it prevailing-religion status.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Greek nationalism stresses a unitary nation-state and treats minorities as religious minorities within it.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Greek nationalists invoke self-determination for Cyprus but reject plebiscite logic for Macedonia and the Aegean, so it is split.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Post-1923 nationalism defends existing borders, yet enosis and the Megali Idea sought to redraw them; split.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Greek nationalism rests on continuity with and devotion to the ancestral Greek lands, from the 1822 Epidauros declaration to the Megali Idea.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: The Megali Idea aimed to bring unredeemed Greeks into the state, and post-1974 nationalism backs Cyprus and Greeks abroad.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Taxation is outside the nationalist program; adherents split between market and state-welfare views.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Social policy is not part of the program and nationalist parties are split between universal and targeted welfare.

material-over-identity.rationale: The movement is built on identity: language, Orthodoxy and continuity with ancient Greece and Byzantium, as the language question and Megali Idea show.

missingStatements.text: A state should object to a neighbouring state using a name or symbols tied to its own historical heritage.
missingStatements.rationale: Greece refused the name Macedonia and the Vergina Sun for its neighbour, treating them as appropriation of Greek heritage and an implied territorial claim.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to the Macedonia naming dispute; not a general question other ideologies would answer meaningfully.

missingStatements.text: A nation's identity runs in unbroken continuity from its ancient origins to the present.
missingStatements.rationale: Greek nationalism links ancient Greece, Byzantium and the modern state as one nation, with Byzantine emperors described as Greek.

notes: Golden Dawn and Metaxas strands would answer more authoritarian and racial questions differently. Irredentist answers reflect the post-1923 defensive consensus.
